Only A is labeled red and H blue, shown as badges. Each unlabeled node takes the average of its neighbors' class scores, so A's group is predicted red (accent color) and H's group blue (teal), as the card lists." width="100%"} Given a few labeled nodes (stored in the node attribute `label_name`), semi-supervised node classification guesses the labels of all the others from the network: nodes that are well connected to nodes of one class probably belong to it too. The harmonic function method (Zhu, Ghahramani and Lafferty, 2003) makes each unlabeled node's class scores the average of its neighbors' scores, with the labeled nodes held fixed, which is the same as asking where a random walk from the node is most likely to first hit a labeled node. Uses include inferring the function of unannotated genes, the topic of uncited papers, or the political leaning of accounts from a small labeled sample. The graph must be undirected. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [label_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["label"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Node attribute holding the known labels (default `"label"`); nodes without it (or with `None`) are unlabeled. Any hashable values can be labels. [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[30]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of propagation steps (default 30). [weighted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Whether to propagate along edge weights. If `None` (default), follows the graph's `weighted` flag. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The predicted label of every node (labeled nodes keep theirs), keyed by node ID. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is directed or no node is labeled. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} With the row-normalized adjacency $P = D^{-1} A$ (labeled rows set to zero) and $B$ the one-hot matrix of known labels, $F \leftarrow P F + B$ is iterated `max_iter` times from $F = 0$, and each node takes the class with the largest score. This is NetworkX's `harmonic_function` exactly; nodes whose top scores tie exactly (for example, nodes equally far from two labels) go to the class seen first in node ID order, where NetworkX's choice depends on rounding. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In two groups joined by one edge, one labeled node per group labels its whole group: ::: {#18861f21 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(list("ABCDEFGH")) g.add_edges( [("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "C"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("E", "F"), ("E", "G"), ("E", "H"), ("F", "G"), ("F", "H"), ("G", "H"), ("D", "E")] ) g.set_node_attrs("label", {g.get_id_from_label("A"): "red", g.get_id_from_label("H"): "blue"}) predicted = g.harmonic_function() {g.get_label_from_id(n): label for n, label in predicted.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'A': 'red', 'B': 'red', 'C': 'red', 'D': 'red', 'E': 'blue', 'F': 'blue', 'G': 'blue', 'H': 'blue'} ``` ::: :::
